body:
What is a semiconductor?

A semiconductor is a material whose electrical conductivity lies between that of a good conductor and that of an insulator, and whose ability to conduct electricity can be controlled under suitable conditions. Silicon is a widely used semiconductor material.

Metals such as copper readily conduct electricity, while insulating materials such as rubber strongly resist its flow under ordinary conditions. Semiconductor materials are especially useful because electronic devices can control their electrical behaviour.

In a basic electric circuit, current flows through a complete conducting path. An open switch interrupts the path. Electronic components extend this simple principle by controlling how electrical signals or currents behave within a device.

Common semiconductor devices

Diode

A diode is an electronic component that ordinarily allows current to pass much more readily in one direction than in the reverse direction. Diodes are used, for example, in converting alternating-current signals into direct-current signals in suitable circuits.

Light-emitting diode

A light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor diode that emits light when operated correctly. LEDs are used in indicators, displays and lighting. Compared with a traditional filament bulb, an LED can produce visible light with a relatively small current.

Transistor

A transistor is a semiconductor device that can act as an electronic switch or amplifier. Switching is particularly important in computers because electronic circuits use controlled states to represent and process information.

Integrated circuit

An integrated circuit (IC) contains many electronic components and their connections formed together on a small piece of semiconductor material. An electronic chip is commonly an IC or another semiconductor device prepared for use in equipment.

Some chips perform calculations or control operations. Others store information. For example, DRAM is used as working memory in electronic systems, while NAND flash is a form of non-volatile storage that retains data without continuous power.

A semiconductor is a material; a transistor is a semiconductor device; an integrated circuit combines electronic components into a functional circuit. These terms do not mean the same thing.

From chip design to an electronic product

Semiconductor production involves several distinct stages. The most important examination distinction is between making circuits on a wafer and preparing fabricated chips for practical use.

  1. Chip design: engineers determine the functions and arrangement of the electronic circuit.
  2. Wafer fabrication: a semiconductor fabrication plant, or fab, forms electronic circuits on semiconductor wafers.
  3. Assembly and packaging: fabricated chips are separated where required, connected and enclosed in suitable packages so that they can be used in equipment.
  4. Testing: electrical and functional checks determine whether a device meets the applicable requirements.
  5. Electronics manufacturing: finished semiconductor devices are incorporated into circuit boards, phones, vehicles, machines and other products.

Fab, ATMP and OSAT

ATMP stands for Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging. These are activities used to prepare and verify semiconductor devices after fabrication.

OSAT stands for Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test. An OSAT facility provides assembly and testing services, often for other companies. ATMP describes a group of processes; OSAT describes an outsourced business or facility performing such work.

A chip-fabrication plant and an ATMP/OSAT plant may both be important semiconductor manufacturing investments, but they do not perform identical work. A packaging facility does not automatically become a wafer-fabrication facility.

Why these stages matter to Gujarat

Gujarat has attracted both wafer-fabrication projects and assembly-and-testing projects. Understanding the production chain makes it possible to distinguish the proposed fab at Dholera from major packaging and testing operations at Sanand and Surat.

Prelims focus

  • Silicon is a commonly used semiconductor material.
  • A diode generally conducts much more readily in one direction; a transistor can function as an electronic switch.
  • IC stands for integrated circuit.
  • A semiconductor fab creates circuits on wafers.
  • ATMP means Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging; OSAT means Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test.
  • Trap: Chip packaging and testing are not the same as front-end wafer fabrication.

[NCERT, Science, Class 6, Electricity and Circuits, pp. 117–120, consulted textbook edition marked 2018–19; NCERT, Science, Class 8, Chemical Effects of Electric Current, pp. 173–175, especially p. 174 on LEDs, consulted textbook edition marked 2018–19; Press Information Bureau, Cabinet Approval of Three Semiconductor Units, 29 February 2024; Press Information Bureau, SEMICON India 2026, 17 September 2026; consulted 5 November 2026.]

body:
Why governments support electronics manufacturing

Electronic devices are used in communication, transport, healthcare, agriculture, industry and public administration. Their production depends on a chain of suppliers that provide semiconductor devices, components, materials, equipment and skilled labour.

Setting up a semiconductor fab or a large electronics facility requires substantial investment and dependable infrastructure. Public policies therefore aim to attract investment, reduce infrastructure difficulties, support training and encourage domestic production.

India Semiconductor Mission and the Semicon India Programme

The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) is a national initiative associated with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The government announced the Semicon India Programme in 2021 with a financial outlay of ₹76,000 crore to support the semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystem.

The programme covers support for activities including semiconductor fabrication, display fabrication, certain specialised semiconductor facilities, assembly and testing, and chip-design capabilities through the applicable national schemes.

In September 2026, the Union government presented Semicon 2.0 as a further expansion of the national ecosystem-building effort, with a stated outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore. Its emphasis extends beyond chip plants to design, equipment and materials, fabrication, advanced packaging, research and workforce development.

These are national programmes. Gujarat's semiconductor and electronics policies are state-level measures intended to attract and facilitate eligible activities within Gujarat. An announced programme outlay is not the same as money already spent on completed factories.

Gujarat Semiconductor Policy (2022–27)

The Gujarat Semiconductor Policy (2022–27) focuses on creating suitable conditions for semiconductor and display-related projects in the state.

It provides a framework for facilitating eligible projects through measures concerning industrial land, access to infrastructure and utilities, approvals and applicable state incentives. Its purpose is to complement the national semiconductor manufacturing effort and attract investments to Gujarat.

Semiconductor projects depend on reliable supplies of electricity and water, transport links, suitable industrial land and supporting businesses. State facilitation is therefore important even when the central government provides financial support.

Gujarat Electronics Policy (2022–28)

The Gujarat Electronics Policy (2022–28) addresses the wider electronics industry, not only semiconductor wafer fabrication. It aims to promote electronics manufacturing, investment, innovation and employment in the state.

The wider sector is often described as Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM). It includes developing and producing electronic systems, components and equipment. A factory assembling an electronic product and a specialised fab producing chips are both associated with electronics, but they occupy different stages of the production chain.

Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy–2025

On 22 June 2025, the Gujarat Department of Science and Technology issued the Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy–2025. It is connected with the wider effort to strengthen the manufacture of electronic components and sub-assemblies.

Examples of components used in electronic products include printed circuit boards, capacitors, connectors and semiconductor devices. Producing more components domestically can support industries that assemble finished electronic products.

Gujarat State Electronics Mission

The Gujarat State Electronics Mission (GSEM) is a state institution focused on developing the electronics, semiconductor, display, design and innovation ecosystem.

Its functions include facilitating investment, supporting electronics manufacturing clusters, promoting innovation and cooperating with industry and educational institutions on skills. GSEM is a state-level facilitator; ISM is a national mission.

From industrial investment to practical applications

The need for an electronics ecosystem becomes clear from its uses:

  • Transport: semiconductor devices help control electronic functions in vehicles and electric-vehicle systems.
  • Telecommunications: chips and circuits support mobile devices and communication equipment.
  • Electricity and industry: electronic systems are used in smart meters, monitoring equipment and industrial controls.
  • Healthcare: electronic devices support measurement, monitoring and medical equipment.
  • Agriculture: sensors and electronic control equipment can support irrigation monitoring and other farm applications.

The benefits of a large semiconductor investment may therefore extend beyond its own factory through suppliers, trained workers, transport services and industries that consume chips.

Prelims focus

  • The Semicon India Programme was announced in 2021 with an outlay of ₹76,000 crore.
  • Semicon 2.0 was presented in September 2026 with a stated outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore.
  • Gujarat Semiconductor Policy: 2022–27.
  • Gujarat Electronics Policy: 2022–28.
  • Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy–2025 was issued on 22 June 2025.
  • Trap: ISM is national; GSEM is a Gujarat institution. Semiconductor policy and wider electronics policy have different scopes.

[Department of Science and Technology, Government of Gujarat, Gujarat Semiconductor Policy (2022–27), Objectives and Support Framework; Gujarat Electronics Policy (2022–28), Policy Overview; Gujarat Electronics Component Manufacturing Policy–2025, Government Resolution dated 22 June 2025; Gujarat State Electronics Mission, Overview; Press Information Bureau, Semicon India Programme, policy and project information; Press Information Bureau, SEMICON India 2026, releases dated 17 and 19 September 2026; consulted 5 November 2026.]

body:
Three important industrial locations

Gujarat's semiconductor investment activity is particularly associated with Sanand, Dholera and Surat. These locations are important for different types of semiconductor work.

Sanand is a major location for semiconductor assembly, testing and packaging projects. Dholera includes planned semiconductor fabrication and display-related facilities. Surat is associated with an outsourced semiconductor assembly and testing project.

The 6 Gujarat projects approved under Semicon India 1.0

By 5 May 2026, Union government announcements identified 12 approved semiconductor manufacturing projects under the first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, of which 6 were in Gujarat.

The following comparison uses approval information and subsequent government production announcements available up to the 5 November 2026 content cutoff. Investment amounts are stated or approximately rounded project outlays. They are not measures of expenditure already completed.

Project and locationPrincipal activityApproved investmentDocumented status
Micron Technology, SanandMemory-chip assembly, testing and packaging₹22,516 croreProduction began 28 February 2026
Tata Electronics with PSMC, DholeraSemiconductor wafer fabricationAbout ₹91,000 croreUnder construction as reported 17 September 2026
CG Power / CG Semi, SanandOutsourced semiconductor assembly and testingAbout ₹7,600 croreCommercial production began 4 July 2026
Kaynes Semicon, SanandOutsourced semiconductor assembly and testing₹3,307 croreProduction began 31 March 2026
Crystal Matrix, DholeraCompound semiconductor fabrication and Mini/Micro-LED display-related manufacturing₹3,068 croreApproved 5 May 2026; proposed facility
Suchi Semicon, SuratOutsourced semiconductor assembly and testing₹868 croreCommercial production line inaugurated 17 September 2026

Understanding the major projects

Micron at Sanand

Micron's project concerns the assembly and testing of semiconductor memory and storage products, including DRAM and NAND technologies. The project was approved in June 2023. Its production launch on 28 February 2026 represents a transition from an approved investment to a producing facility.

Tata Electronics and PSMC at Dholera

Tata Electronics' project involves a wafer-fabrication plant developed with Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC), Taiwan. It was approved in February 2024.

The proposed capacity is approximately 50,000 wafer starts per month. This describes planned wafer-processing capacity, not the number of finished chips currently produced.

On 9 April 2026, an associated special economic zone at Dholera received government notification. The notification was reported on 16 April 2026. A special economic zone is a legally designated area with an applicable administrative and regulatory framework; its notification is not proof that a fabrication plant has begun commercial production.

A government release dated 17 September 2026 described the Dholera fab as under construction. It should therefore not be grouped with Gujarat's operating commercial packaging facilities merely because the project has been approved and construction is progressing.

CG Semi and Kaynes at Sanand

CG Power's project, with technology and investment partners including Renesas and Stars Microelectronics, was approved in February 2024. Its facility entered commercial production on 4 July 2026.

Kaynes Semicon's Sanand project was approved in September 2024. Its production began on 31 March 2026, after Micron but before CG Semi.

Crystal Matrix at Dholera

On 5 May 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Crystal Matrix project for an integrated compound semiconductor and display-related facility at Dholera. It includes gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor technology for Mini/Micro-LED applications.

GaN is a semiconductor material. The project differs from the Tata–PSMC silicon wafer fab because it targets different materials and applications. Approval describes a planned investment, not an operating display-production line.

Suchi Semicon at Surat

Suchi Semicon received central approval for an OSAT project at Surat in May 2026. Its intended applications include devices for power electronics, vehicles, industrial systems and consumer electronics.

At SEMICON India 2026, a commercial production line at Suchi Semicon, Surat, was inaugurated on 17 September 2026. This is a significant status change: an earlier description of the project as merely approved would be incomplete after that date.

How to interpret investment and capacity figures

Approval means the relevant proposal has received official clearance. Construction means the facility is being developed. Commercial production means production has begun for commercial purposes. These are different stages.

Likewise, a proposed capacity is not actual output. Wafer starts per month and packaged chips per day measure different production activities and cannot be directly compared as though they were identical units.

Gujarat–Assam distinction: The Tata Electronics–PSMC wafer fab is at Dholera, Gujarat. Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test's separately approved ATMP project is at Morigaon, Assam. The projects should not be confused.

Prelims focus

  • Micron: Sanand, ATMP, approved June 2023; production began 28 February 2026.
  • Tata Electronics–PSMC: Dholera, wafer fab, approved February 2024; under construction in September 2026.
  • CG Semi: Sanand, OSAT; commercial production began 4 July 2026.
  • Kaynes Semicon: Sanand, OSAT; production began 31 March 2026.
  • Crystal Matrix: Dholera, compound semiconductor and Mini/Micro-LED project; approved May 2026. Suchi Semicon: Surat, OSAT; commercial line inaugurated September 2026.
  • Trap: An approved investment, an SEZ notification and an operating production line represent different facts.

[Press Information Bureau, Cabinet Approval of Three Semiconductor Units, 29 February 2024; Press Information Bureau, semiconductor project approvals and investment information, 2025–2026; Press Information Bureau, Government Notifies India's First Chip Fabrication Plant at SEZ Dholera, 16 April 2026; Press Information Bureau, Cabinet Approves Two More Semiconductor Manufacturing Units, 5 May 2026; Press Information Bureau, Micron and Kaynes production announcements, 28 February and 31 March 2026; Press Information Bureau, CG Semi Commercial Production, 4 July 2026; Press Information Bureau, SEMICON India 2026, 17 and 19 September 2026; The Indian Express, Cabinet Clears Two Chip Plants Worth ₹3,936 Crore, 6 May 2026; consulted 5 November 2026.]
